oidc_jwt.description: Returned scope on token and token-exchange responses may differ from the provided scope parameter.
oidc_jwt.source: OpenID/OAuth endpoints docs: token endpoint and token exchange response tables
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag scope-string differences alone as privilege escalation; inspect actual claims/audience and whether returned scope exceeds documented authorization context.

oidc_jwt.description: Introspection returns active=true only when the token is active and the requesting client is part of the token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: active=false for a valid token from a non-audience client is by design, not a token-validation failure.

oidc_jwt.description: The userinfo response only contains claims corresponding to granted scopes; absent optional claims are expected when scopes were not requested.
oidc_jwt.note: Prevents false positives when comparing expected identity metadata or authorization-derived claims.

oidc_jwt.description: Token exchange rejects requested scopes that exceed the scope granted by the resource owner with invalid_scope.
oidc_jwt.note: Scope-expansion rejection is expected behavior, not a bug.

oidc_jwt.description: UserInfo returns claims only depending on granted scopes; minimal responses may contain only sub and a subset of profile fields.
oidc_jwt.source: userinfo endpoint and claims matrix docs
oidc_jwt.note: Missing email/profile/groups-like claims is by design when scopes were not granted.

oidc_jwt.description: The userinfo endpoint only accepts an access token of the user, not the client.
oidc_jwt.note: Using a client/service token against userinfo and getting failure or sparse claims is by design.

oidc_jwt.description: Introspection returns active=true only when the token is active and the requesting client is part of the token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: An inactive introspection result can reflect audience mismatch rather than revocation or expiry.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT bearer grant documentation does not promise jti replay tracking or one-time assertion use.
oidc_jwt.source: grant types and token endpoint JWT profile docs
oidc_jwt.note: Reusing the same valid JWT assertion is not automatically a vulnerability in this platform profile.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT profile grant authenticates service accounts/machines rather than interactive end-users.
oidc_jwt.source: grant-types.mdx and endpoints.mdx JWT Profile Grant sections
oidc_jwt.note: Do not compare machine-token identity behavior to human user login expectations.

oidc_jwt.description: Unsupported response_mode values on the authorization endpoint are ignored.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag fallback to default response mode as a flow-coherence bug.

oidc_jwt.description: The redirect_uri in the token request must exactly match the redirect_uri used in the authorization request.
oidc_jwt.source: endpoints.mdx authorization code grant and end_session docs
oidc_jwt.note: Mismatch failures are by design and should not be treated as flow confusion.
Failures with other PKCE methods are expected unsupported-method behavior.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against login_with_jwt, the JWT bearer assertion MUST include aud containing the ZITADEL issuing domain, iss=sub matching the service account or client key owner, and a kid header matching the downloaded keyId. Otherwise token rejection is ambiguous and may reflect malformed client authentication rather than freshness enforcement.

For JWT assertions used in login_with_jwt and private_key_jwt client authentication, iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. Use iat={{now_epoch}} for control tokens. Tokens with stale iat can fail independently of exp/nbf, so freshness tests must isolate one time claim at a time.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, the sequence MUST include a CONTROL login using a valid JWT assertion with iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} alongside the ATTACK login. Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED cannot be distinguished from wrong aud/iss/sub/kid or unsupported client authentication setup.

ZITADEL documents replay protection via nonce for browser implicit/auth requests, but JWT bearer grant documentation does NOT mention jti tracking or one-time-use enforcement. Do NOT treat replay_same_token or stateless_jwt_no_jti on login_with_jwt as an I2 vulnerability by itself; JWT bearer assertions are not documented as single-use.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, exchange_code_for_token MUST send the exact same redirect_uri used in start_oidc_auth. ZITADEL requires exact match and returns invalid_grant when the redirection URI differs, which is by design and should be asserted as flow binding rather than identity mismatch.

For I3 state_swap tests, start_oidc_auth SHOULD always include a unique state value and the test oracle must compare returned state to the sent value. Missing state weakens the test because ZITADEL only recommends, not requires, state for CSRF mitigation.

For OIDC implicit-flow requests via start_oidc_auth, nonce MUST be provided. ZITADEL states nonce MUST be provided when using implicit flow. Missing nonce causes request failure unrelated to the security property under test.

For PKCE-based code flow tests, code_challenge_method supports only exact value S256. Do not fuzz alternate methods expecting negotiation; unsupported methods fail by design. For pkce_skip and related checks, assert non-200/error outcomes rather than identity differences.

For token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. Rejections caused by requesting an audience outside that subset are by documented policy and must not be misclassified as broader token-exchange bugs.

For token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, requested scope on token_exchange MUST be interpreted relative to the subject token and ZITADEL may return scopes that differ from the requested scope. The oracle must inspect returned scope and claims, not assume echo semantics.

For token_exchange tests using actor_token, actor_token_type is required whenever actor_token is provided. Omitting actor_token_type yields malformed-request behavior unrelated to delegation or impersonation security.

Token exchange token-type parameters are exact identifiers only. Supported values are documented as urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token, urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token, urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt, and urn:zitadel:params:oauth:token-type:user_id with specific restrictions. Do NOT use wildcards or partial matches; these parameters have exact-match semantics.

For I5 token_exchange tests, requested_token_type has documented restrictions: access_token subject tokens can yield opaque tokens only, jwt requested_token_type is only for specific combinations, and refresh_token is not allowed in the token-type matrix. Failures from unsupported combinations are by design.

Introspection success depends on the requesting client being part of the token audience. A false active or 401 invalid_client can result from wrong client authentication or wrong audience, not token invalidity. Use the same audience-bound client when validating freshness or revocation via introspect_token.

userinfo_endpoint accepts only access tokens of a user, not client-only tokens. Do NOT use verify_granted_identity with client_credentials-style or service-account-only access tokens expecting user claims; use introspect_token for machine-token inspection instead.
ZITADEL does not support Resource Owner Password Credentials grant. login_with_password is absent for this protocol run and must not be scheduled.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against login_with_jwt, the JWT profile assertion MUST include aud containing the ZITADEL issuing domain, iss=sub matching the service account userId, a kid header matching the downloaded keyId, and iat no older than 1 hour. Otherwise token rejection is ambiguous and may reflect malformed client authentication rather than freshness enforcement.

For I2 token-freshness tests on login_with_jwt, include a CONTROL login using a valid assertion with iat={{now_epoch}}, exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}, aud set to the ZITADEL issuer domain, and matching iss/sub. Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED on the attack assertion cannot be distinguished from broken JWT-profile setup.

For I1 trust-anchor and key-rotation tests on login_with_jwt, ZITADEL identifies the signing key by the JWT header kid and validates against the downloaded key for the service account/application. The fuzzer MUST vary kid consistently with the signing key under test; a mismatched or missing kid causes lookup failure rather than a pure signature-validation result.

For I3 code-flow coherence tests, exchange_code_for_token with grant_type=authorization_code MUST use the exact same redirect_uri as start_oidc_auth. A mismatch is documented to produce invalid_grant/invalid_request behavior and is not evidence of a broker flaw.

For PKCE-based code flow tests, start_oidc_auth MUST send code_challenge and code_challenge_method=S256, and exchange_code_for_token MUST send the matching plaintext code_verifier plus client_id. ZITADEL documents S256 as the only supported PKCE method; other methods fail by design.

For private_key_jwt client authentication on exchange_code_for_token, token_exchange, introspect_token, or revoke_session, the client_assertion JWT MUST include aud containing the ZITADEL issuing domain, iss=sub equal to clientId, exp, and iat not older than 1 hour, plus kid equal to the downloaded keyId. Failures here are client-authentication failures, not target invariant violations.

For token_exchange I5 audience-binding tests, requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from both subject_token and actor_token. If the requested audience exceeds that set, rejection is by design and must not be reported as a vulnerability.

For token_exchange I5 scope-escalation tests, requested scope on token exchange is constrained by OAuth semantics and documented invalid_scope behavior. The fuzzer MUST compare exchanged-token claims/scopes against the original authorization and treat invalid_scope rejection as compliant behavior, not a failure.

For token_exchange type tests, subject_token_type and requested_token_type are restricted by ZITADEL's documented matrix: access_token subject tokens may yield opaque access tokens only; refresh_token is not allowed; id_token is allowed; jwt subject_token is allowed only when combined with actor_token; user_id subject_token is allowed only when combined with actor_token. Unsupported combinations must be treated as setup errors, not security findings.

For verify_granted_identity, /oidc/v1/userinfo only accepts an access_token of a user as Bearer token, not a client-only token. JWT-profile service-account access tokens may not yield human userinfo semantics; use introspect_token as the control inspection path for machine-token tests to avoid false I4 conclusions.

For introspect_token and revoke_session, client authentication is required by documentation ('depending on your authorization method'). The fuzzer MUST authenticate as the token's client using either client_secret_basic/body credentials or private_key_jwt; otherwise 401 invalid_client is expected and not evidence about token validity or revocation state.

For start_oidc_auth, response_mode invalid values are ignored by design. Tests that rely on a specific response transport MUST explicitly request a supported mode (query, fragment, or form_post) and verify the returned mode accordingly; do not treat fallback behavior as flow confusion.

For start_oidc_auth, implicit flow requires nonce and code flow strongly recommends state/nonce. I3 state-swap tests MUST include a distinct state per browser session and compare returned state exactly; missing state makes the test inconclusive because CSRF/session binding was not exercised.

For reserved-scope authorization tests, ZITADEL-specific scopes actively change authorization semantics. In particular, urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} enforces organization membership, urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} enforces membership plus username suffix, and urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud adds that project to token audience. The fuzzer MUST account for these scope side effects when interpreting I4/I5 outcomes.

For I5 audience tests, ZITADEL access-token aud by default includes all client IDs and the project ID, and additional audiences can be added via reserved scopes. The fuzzer MUST inspect actual aud via introspect_token instead of assuming a single audience value.

For I1 key-identification tests on login_with_jwt and private_key_jwt-authenticated token/introspection calls, the JWT header MUST include kid equal to the downloaded keyId. ZITADEL uses kid to identify the key; missing or wrong kid can fail before the intended signature/trust test and confound results.

For I2 replay_same_token on login_with_jwt, do NOT treat successful reuse of the same JWT-profile assertion as a documented vulnerability unless the docs explicitly promise one-time assertion tracking. The provided docs describe stateless JWT profile validation requirements but do not document jti replay prevention.

For I3 state_swap and other OIDC flow-coherence tests, start_oidc_auth SHOULD include a state value and the test oracle MUST verify the returned state is the unmodified request state. Omitting state removes the documented CSRF/session-binding signal and makes swap tests invalid.

For OIDC implicit-flow or hybrid authorize tests, nonce MUST be supplied when response_type includes id_token, and for robust control cases it SHOULD also be supplied on code flow. Missing nonce can cause failures unrelated to the intended attack or remove replay-binding semantics.
For PKCE-based code-flow tests, code_challenge_method supports only S256. Do not send plain or alternate methods; failures would be by-design unsupported-method behavior, not a flow-coherence bug.

For redirect_uri_mismatch tests, exchange_code_for_token MUST use exactly the same redirect_uri as start_oidc_auth in control cases. ZITADEL documents exact matching between authorization and token requests; mismatches are expected invalid_grant behavior.

For token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, audience in token_exchange MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from both subject and actor tokens in control cases. Requests outside that subset are documented to fail by design and should not be reported as unexpected tightening.

For token_exchange token-type tests, respect ZITADEL's documented token type matrix: subject_token_type access_token accepts JWT or opaque; id_token is allowed; jwt is allowed only when combined with actor_token; refresh_token is not allowed; user_id is allowed only with actor_token. Unsupported combinations are by-design failures.

For token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, use a control where requested scope is equal to or narrower than the original authorization. ZITADEL documents invalid_scope when requested scope exceeds the scope granted by the resource owner; such rejection is expected and should not be misclassified.

For introspect_token tests, active=true is only returned when the requesting client is authorized and is part of the token audience. A false/401 result can reflect client-audience mismatch rather than token invalidity; use the same audience-bound client in control and attack cases.

For verify_granted_identity and other API calls using the session token, session_token MUST be the access_token, not the id_token. ZITADEL's userinfo endpoint explicitly requires the access token of the user as Bearer token.

For I5 scope/claim tests using verify_granted_identity, claims returned by /oidc/v1/userinfo depend on granted scopes. Missing email/profile/roles/resourceowner/metadata claims without the corresponding scopes is by design; include the relevant scopes in control requests before asserting claim presence or absence.

For I5 audience tests, note that ZITADEL access-token aud by default includes all client IDs and the project ID, and additional audiences can be requested via reserved scopes such as urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud. Control cases must account for these defaults before concluding audience over-grant.

For I2 control cases on login_with_jwt, use exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} and iat={{now_epoch}} to satisfy the documented 'iat must not be older than 1h' rule while keeping the assertion valid. Attack cases should vary only the freshness claim under test.
